title: Zillow and Redfin settle FTC antitrust case over rental-listing market competition
summary: Zillow and Redfin have settled an antitrust case with the FTC and five states regarding a 2025 partnership that allegedly reduced competition in the rental-listing market. The FTC claimed the deal, where Zillow paid Redfin $100 million to avoid direct competition, could have led to higher prices and lower-quality listings for consumers. The settlement requires Redfin to reenter the rental advertising business and removes restrictions on its ability to compete independently.
key_points: Zillow and Redfin settled an FTC antitrust case over a 2025 partnership that allegedly harmed competition in the rental-listing market.
The FTC argued that Zillow paid Redfin $100 million to avoid competition, potentially leading to higher prices and reduced service quality for property managers and consumers.
The settlement requires Redfin to reenter the rental advertising business and removes previous restrictions on its ability to compete independently.
Redfin can still display Zillow’s rental listings but will now compete for its own customers without sharing sensitive business information.
The case follows a broader trend of antitrust enforcement, similar to the DOJ’s recent actions against Ticketmaster and Live Nation.
